layers.note: A tall herb of moist meadows, stream banks and open woods.

heat_load.note: Cool aspects more than hot ones.

elevation_m.note: Lowlands in the north to subalpine.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −20 to 2 °C; gone below −30 °C and above 6 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 9 to 20 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 24 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 800 to 4,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500.

degree_days_5.note: About 250 to 2,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Tall bluebells grow from Alaska to Oregon and east across Canada (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
